tldr: MPP adds a Payment authentication scheme to HTTP 402. The server sends a challenge, the client pays through a named method and retries with a credential, and the server returns a receipt.
whyItExists: An agent that wants one API call, one page of data or a stream of model tokens should not need an account, an API key and a card on file first. MPP puts the price and the proof of payment into the ordinary HTTP authentication headers, so a client can pay on the first request. Because the core says nothing about money movement, the same challenge and credential shape works for stablecoins on Tempo and other chains, Stripe Shared Payment Tokens, card network tokens (the card method written by Visa) and Lightning, and each rail writes its own method.

whatItIsNot.text: Not Stripe-only. Tempo Labs and Stripe co-author the core, and Visa, Lightspark, Circle, Coinbase and others author payment methods.
Not an IETF standard. The core is an individual Internet-Draft with no working group, no stream and no intended status, and IANA has registered none of its names.

Not crypto-only. Methods cover cards through Stripe Shared Payment Tokens and through the card method written by Visa, which carries encrypted network tokens from Visa, Mastercard, American Express or Discover, plus Bitcoin over Lightning.
Not the MPP of AP2. In AP2 documents, MPP means Merchant Payment Processor, an unrelated role.

Not a standardized session intent. Only charge and subscription are in specs/intents; session is defined inside method specs. Generic session pull requests closed unmerged on 2026-09-28 and 2026-11-07, and a third was still open on 2026-11-21.
Not x402. The two are separate HTTP 402 designs with a documented mapping, and the mppx SDK can serve both on one route.

Not an identity or mandate protocol. The core has no agent identity and no user mandate: its credential carries only the challenge echo, an optional payer source and the method payload. Since 2026-11-11 its repository text says how other authentication combines with Payment without defining any, and identity checks are an optional mppx SDK feature.

changedRecently.text: At IETF 127 the HTTP working group heard a draft that would define only the meaning of status 402. Its slides list MPP's core draft among current uses, and a show of hands on adoption interest gave 15 yes, 3 no and 18 no opinion.

mppx 0.21.0 fixed payment-boundary flaws without an advisory, among them one payment authorizing a second response and a Zone settlement paying twice, and made proxy replay need a stable replay.authority; 0.21.1 added a helper for Tempo's x402 facilitator.

Tempo's x402 facilitator, which takes USDC on Base and pays sellers in OUSD on Tempo, gained helpers in mppx 0.21.1 and pympp 0.26.0, a day after its docs merged; buyers pay Tempo's deposit address, so sellers rely on Tempo for the payout.

Node release tempo/v1.19.0 scheduled Tempo's T14 upgrade (testnet 2026-11-24, mainnet 2026-12-08). A payer that moves to a configurable account cannot top up older channels or sign its own session vouchers under T14.

The pympp advisory GHSA-v858-xh7w-8jr5 entered the GitHub Advisory Database as medium, and the author of a pull request that would have moved MPP's MCP binding off error codes that MCP reserves closed it unmerged.

mppx 0.19.1 added a Poppy identity provider and 0.20.0 an ERC-8004 identity provider, an SDK feature that no MPP draft specifies; 0.20.0 also fixed session metering and payer flaws, with breaking changes.
mppx 0.19.0 made the Web Bot Auth and TAP provers take key pairs or remote signers instead of private keys.
The core -01 was edited in place with rules for combining Payment with other authentication, including a second meaning for 403; the IETF copy of -01 was not updated.
mppx 0.18.0 gave identity checks fixed statuses (a missing proof now gets 401, not 403) and made the Tempo server methods refuse to start in production without an explicitly configured store.
mppx 0.17.4 let a payer pay a Tempo charge from a private Zone balance, four days after Tempo's T13 upgrade put the Zones prover on mainnet.
mppx 0.16.0 replaced request attestation with per-route identity verifiers, a breaking change that moved the TAP and Web Bot Auth modules.
A Solana subscription method merged, so subscription now has three method profiles; the same day a Tempo maintainer closed six external method proposals as too small for the official spec.
mppx 0.14.0 added idempotency keys and credits for Tempo session charges and stopped settle() from capturing a voucher above spent; 0.14.1 followed the same day.
Mastercard opened Agent Pay for Machines Early Access with a brief that builds the product on x402 and names no MPP.
mppx 0.13.5 began answering a replayed or already-claimed Tempo charge credential with a final 403 and no new challenge. This is SDK behavior, not part of the draft.
mpp-specs issue #374 flagged that the MCP transport's error codes -32042 and -32043 collide with MCP's own codes; it was still open on 2026-11-21.
The pull request for a generic session intent closed without merging; session stays defined per method.
The core draft's repository text moved the optional header slot of the recommended HMAC binding before opaque; the posted -01 appends it last, so the layouts differ only when header is present.
draft-httpauth-payment-01 posted; it is a new revision, not a rename. The old draft name expired on 2026-09-18.
XRPL charge and session methods merged, bringing the spec repository to 11 method ids.
mppx 0.9.0 added dual MPP and x402 wrappers for Express, Hono, Next.js and MCP.
The header challenge parameter and the Payment-Authorization field merged, so a credential can travel next to a bearer token.
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments added MPP at general availability: AgentCore pays MPP charge challenges for agents, where its 2026-05-07 preview described only x402.
The subscription intent merged with Stripe and Tempo subscription methods.
Tempo session v2, on the TIP-20 channel escrow precompile, merged into the session spec (blog post 2026-06-17).
draft-httpauth-payment-00 appeared on the IETF Datatracker under a new name while draft-ryan-httpauth-payment-01 was still active.
AWS WAF's AI traffic monetization launched with x402 only, and AWS said MPP support was coming soon; the WAF guide read on 2026-11-21 still names only x402.
